Aug 28OUTBOUND DAYMedium-low confidenceAug 28 · 06:00–22:00 ET
METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KLZU observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. KLZU has no TAF station, so KPDK is used as a proxy. It is the strongest flight-category evidence this page can show. Beyond the TAF horizon of about 30 hours; no TAF exists at this range for any station.NWS-hrNWS hourly gridpoint forecast — the National Weather Service digital forecast for the grid cell containing KLZU, updated through the day and reaching about 156 hours. It gives hour-by-hour sky, wind and precipitation probability, and it is the spine of the change windows on this board. The NWS hourly gridpoint forecast reaches this day.NWS-dayNWS day/night outlook — the same National Weather Service grid summarised into day and night halves, reaching about 168 hours. Coarser than the hourly product but it covers one day further, so this page uses it only to describe spans the hourly forecast cannot reach. Not needed: this day is already covered by the finer-resolution hourly gridpoint forecast.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued by the National Weather Service four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this page uses it to corroborate the flight category. Beyond the GFS MAV MOS horizon of about 72 hours, or no MAV row carried both a ceiling and a visibility for this day.MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This page shows it only as a flagged outlook and never promotes it into a short-range category. An extended GFS MEX outlook point describes part of this day. MEX publishes no ceiling or visibility, so it states no flight category; where its sky, precipitation, thunderstorm or obstruction fields are usable it is shown as a clearly labelled “(Predicted)” value.GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. The NOTAM query failed this run (state: AUTH_ERROR), so the NOTAM list is unknown rather than empty.

The NWS hourly gridpoint forecast reaches this day.NWS-dayNWS day/night outlook — the same National Weather Service grid summarised into day and night halves, reaching about 168 hours. Coarser than the hourly product but it covers one day further, so this page uses it only to describe spans the hourly forecast cannot reach. Not needed: this day is already covered by the finer-resolution hourly gridpoint forecast.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued by the National Weather Service four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this page uses it to corroborate the flight category. Extended outlook summary

.. (Today through Thursday) Issued at 355 AM EDT Wed Aug 26 2026 A quiet start to what will be a more active period across North and Central Georgia. — .. (Thursday night through Tuesday) Issued at 355 AM EDT Wed Aug 26 2026 Starting off the long term outlook on Friday, the upper level wave break pattern will continue to bring scattered to widespread showers and thunder…

Short term

.. (Today through Thursday) Issued at 355 AM EDT Wed Aug 26 2026 A quiet start to what will be a more active period across North and Central Georgia. Low clouds and patchy fog will fill in across parts of Central Georgia and could briefly develop as far south as the metro through right around sunrise. The forecast area remains within a quasi- NW flow regime. A weak frontal boundary remains draped across Central Georgia, roughly from Columbus to Macon, based on current dewpoint observations. Continued moisture return and instability will support higher coverage of scattered showers and storms this afternoon. CAMs are still all over the place with placement and coverage but it is anticipated that the frontal boundary and the thermal gradient from this morning's cloud cover is likely where convection will get started later today. All storms will be capable of frequent lightning, gusty winds, and locally heavy rainfall. Coverage of showers and storms should decrease following sunset given loss of daytime heating but I imagine isolated activity may linger. Additionally, several hi-res models still indicate a potential MCS (cluster of thunderstorms) tracking southeastward into parts of AL overnight but it's unclear if this will hold together or even make it to NW/W GA. For now maintain low chances (15-20%) for showers and thunderstorms overnight. Midlevel troughing will encompass much of the eastern U.S. and a vort max within the flow will push a cold front towards the forecast area on Thursday. Ample instability, plentiful moisture (PWs 1.7- 2.1") and flow nearly parallel to the incoming boundary will support scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms across all of North and Central GA. Limited shear and high moisture content will mean storms will be slow-moving, heavy rain producers. Thus, locally heavy rainfall and a threat for flash flooding is likely. WPC maintains a Slight Risk (Level 2 of 4) of Excessive Rainfall for much of North GA on Thursday, given recent trends. Depending on how things evolve, a Flood Watch may be needed across parts of North GA. While widespread severe weather remains low through the short-term, high moisture content will result in heavily water-loaded downdrafts with any storms. Thus, strong gusty winds cannot be ruled out. Temperatures will remain fairly seasonable both today and Thursday. This afternoon daytime highs will rise into the 90s (5-10 deg cooler in the mountains) with heat indices in the 100-104F range across Central GA. On Thursday, temperatures will be a few degrees cooler as a result of higher cloud coverage and storm coverage.

Long term

.. (Thursday night through Tuesday) Issued at 355 AM EDT Wed Aug 26 2026 Starting off the long term outlook on Friday, the upper level wave break pattern will continue to bring scattered to widespread showers and thunderstorms to much of north and central GA. PWATs in excess of 2 inches will mean heavy soaking rains may continue from previous days. The overall risk for severe weather through the long term remains fairly low. Thunderstorms on Friday are likely to develop in areas which have already been worked over with limited organization. Moving into the weekend, upper level flow shifts eastward bringing broad ridging back overhead. High temperatures will return to the 90s with dewpoints in the 70s. Just another blast of the summer sauna. Thunderstorms potential drops through the weekend, though isolated to scattered diurnally driven thunderstorms remain possible. PWATs falling below 2 inches will also reduce the risk for flash flooding.

METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KTRI observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. No usable TAF covers the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). A TAF reaches only about 30 hours, so a later trip day being uncovered is a horizon fact, not a fault.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. The NOTAM query failed this run (state: AUTH_ERROR), so the NOTAM list is unknown rather than empty.

KGKT OBS - VFR Gatlinburg-Pigeon Forge Arpt, TN, US · Smokies/GatlinburgETE0h50Dist114 nm
METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KGKT observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. No usable TAF covers the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). A TAF reaches only about 30 hours, so a later trip day being uncovered is a horizon fact, not a fault. This airport has no TAF station of its own, so KTYS is used as a proxy; that is a normal condition, not a failure.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. The NOTAM query failed this run (state: AUTH_ERROR), so the NOTAM list is unknown rather than empty.

METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KSAV observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. No usable TAF covers the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). A TAF reaches only about 30 hours, so a later trip day being uncovered is a horizon fact, not a fault.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A current KSSI observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. Beyond the 30 h TAF horizon at this lead time. METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KFIN observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. No usable TAF covers the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). A TAF reaches only about 30 hours, so a later trip day being uncovered is a horizon fact, not a fault. This airport has no TAF station of its own, so KDAB is used as a proxy; that is a normal condition, not a failure.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KCRE observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. No usable TAF covers the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). A TAF reaches only about 30 hours, so a later trip day being uncovered is a horizon fact, not a fault. This airport has no TAF station of its own, so KMYR is used as a proxy; that is a normal condition, not a failure.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KECP observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. No usable TAF covers the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). A TAF reaches only about 30 hours, so a later trip day being uncovered is a horizon fact, not a fault.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KDAB observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. No usable TAF covers the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). A TAF reaches only about 30 hours, so a later trip day being uncovered is a horizon fact, not a fault.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. KTPF OBS - VFR Tampa/Knight Arpt, FL, US · Tampa Peter O KnightETE2h32Dist372 nm
METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KTPF observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. No usable TAF covers the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). A TAF reaches only about 30 hours, so a later trip day being uncovered is a horizon fact, not a fault. This airport has no TAF station of its own, so KTPA is used as a proxy; that is a normal condition, not a failure.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. The NOTAM query failed this run (state: AUTH_ERROR), so the NOTAM list is unknown rather than empty.

KVNC OBS - VFR Venice Muni, FL, US · Venice FLETE2h51Dist422 nm
METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KVNC observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. No usable TAF covers the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). A TAF reaches only about 30 hours, so a later trip day being uncovered is a horizon fact, not a fault. This airport has no TAF station of its own, so KSRQ is used as a proxy; that is a normal condition, not a failure.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. The NOTAM query failed this run (state: AUTH_ERROR), so the NOTAM list is unknown rather than empty.

A TAF reaches only about 30 hours, so a later trip day being uncovered is a horizon fact, not a fault.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. 3 · Hazard feeds & regional observations

Unfiltered hazard feeds (not route-geometry screened): 10 SIGMET records, 20 G-AIRMET records, 2 CWA records. Regional current observations (not corridor forecasts): Atlantic North: category unavailable at KMYR; Gulf West: category unavailable at KHSA.

4 · Planning gates

  • Evidence gate: an unavailable, stale, or out-of-horizon source is unknown — never treat it as favorable.
  • Weather gate: compare current observations and valid-period forecasts with personal ceiling, visibility, convection, wind, and crosswind minimums.
  • Route gate: screen the actual route, altitude, and time against official hazard products; feed totals on this page are not route-filtered.
  • Operations gate: verify NOTAMs, TFRs, runway conditions, fuel, aircraft performance, daylight, and alternates.

5 · ForeFlight manual cross-check (before flight)

  • Official briefing matches these go/no-go windows
  • Prog charts / radar / satellite trend agrees with convection timing
  • Winds & temps aloft along actual route (may shift ETE)
  • NOTAMs & TFRs — airport-scoped NMS records may be shown, but route-wide/TFR coverage is not included; pull a fresh official briefing for departure, destination, and alternates
  • Runway condition / length / closures at destination & alternate
  • Weight & balance + performance at forecast density altitude (heat!)
  • File & brief in ForeFlight; confirm fuel stops if long-range

Everything the page does

  • Mission Control with destination and day selection, fail-closed category ranges, a keyboard- and touch-operable schematic airport map, filters, clustering, and a synchronized text list
  • Per-source state, validity horizon, and target-date coverage for every destination
  • Explicit unavailable/out-of-horizon target cells; no static weather fallback
  • Per-airport expandable detail — current observations, covered forecasts, dep/dest METAR temperatures
  • Current-and-future KLZU board with four fixed 06:00–22:00 ET boxes and outbound/return day context
  • Source-labelled TAF/MOS flight-category guidance only when a source interval actually covers the visible standard box — a box with no covering interval shows an explicit unavailable/out-of-horizon state instead of a category, never an implied one
  • Timed NWS weather, wind-favored runway (magnetic, from each airport's own runways), gust, and material crosswind context wherever the forecast supplies them
  • Raw METAR/TAF + data-sources dropdown per airport
  • FAA Airport Status & Delays with known, unsupported, and unavailable states
  • Best-effort 100LL fuel prices
  • Auto-refreshed about 4x a day by an hourly scheduler that republishes once 6 h have passed since the last publish, so refresh times drift; the last-updated stamp is exact and the next-run stamp is an estimate
  • Quick links (Flight Circle, ForeFlight, FlightAware) + Feedback
  • FAA chart-cycle stamp (current VFR Sectional + Chart Supplement)
  • Download PDF — print-ready, color-preserving (semantic colors kept on paper)
  • Deterministic evidence-backed page; external AI aviation prose is withheld pending a validated evidence schema, so the executive-summary region shows an explicit pending-feature placeholder instead of generated text
  • Model-labeled MOS target-window outlook per airport (Iowa State GFS with conditional GFS Extended/MEX), with runtime and validity horizon shown
  • Expandable NWS FFC pattern summary and extended outlook inside the KLZU board
  • Per-airport chart links: SkyVector & AirNav/Chart Supplement (deep links)
  • FAA NMS owner-approved production source NOTAM adapter with explicit per-airport source states; reporting an explicit error state rather than an empty list, and never a substitute for an official briefing
  • Full run archive: run_manifest.json with all data + provenance log
